correctness.rationale: Partition configurations on K_{a,b} into empty, left-only, right-only, both-nonempty classes, with exact disjoint weights 1, (1+2z)^a-1, (1+2z)^b-1, 2[(1+z)^a-1][(1+z)^b-1]. For a=n, b=n-floor(kappa sqrt n), z=c/sqrt n, Taylor logs yield three nonzero limiting weights exp(-2c²), exp(-2c²-2kappa c), 2 exp(-c²-kappa c), with empty weight vanishing. Normalizing gives P_B(c)=[1+exp(-c²)cosh(kappa c)]^{-1}. The derivative sign is the negative of -2c+kappa tanh(kappa c); since tanh(t)/t strictly decreases, the exact reentrance threshold is kappa>sqrt2 with a unique minimum c*. Conditional binomial laws and O(sqrt n) variances prove the three-atom count limit. Fixed-c pointwise convergence at three chosen c values proves nonmonotonicity of finite-n probability for all sufficiently large n in the supercritical case. Independent direct enumeration for all 1<=a,b<=3 and z=1/3,2/3 matched exact four-class partition weights. No claim of a thermodynamic phase transition or finite-n monotonicity below threshold.

evidence: The regular-graph occupancy bound concerns average occupied fraction at fixed activity, not event E_B for asymptotically nearly balanced K_{a,b}.
Brightwell et al. 1999 nonmonotonic Gibbs symmetry breaking uses modified Cayley trees, not this finite-volume sector probability.

value.rationale: The precise competition of one-side/two-side occupancy sectors in a canonical high-degree bipartite WR model gives a motivated sharp critical window and previously nonobvious reentrant event-probability threshold. The three distinct normalized occupation-count atoms and the exact uniqueness of the reversal are coherent structural results; they do not purport to be thermodynamic phase transitions. A finite graph count alone would be standard, but the scaling classification is a useful natural asymptotic invariant.

limitations: Not a bounded-degree infinite-volume Gibbs phase transition; limiting result fixed c>0 and fixed kappa.
No joint asymptotic uniformity when c varies with n and no finite-n monotonicity claim for subcritical kappa.
